Several other issues of contemporary relevance and importance have also been raised which are not a subject of discussion for this Bill but because it is leather and it is now of great importance and interest, those have also been added to the debate. I will try to confine myself first to the matters which pertain to the Bill, although it might be useful also to address directly or indirectly some of the questions which have been raised by the hon. Members.

First of all, the need for giving the stature of institute of national importance is something to which I would like to draw the attention of every hon. Member. This institution which till today has only seven centres - some of them are in the pipeline, the rest five will be completed soon - has an all-India presence and has strived hard to provide very good quality content of curricula, as a result of which, students, even if they took certificates initially or degrees later, have been placed in very good jobs and our rate of recruitment has always been high, as a result of which, people have sought admission. Although it is observed by some of the hon. Members that the courses were very highly charged in the sense of the fees as compared to many other institutions considered to be expensive, yet people are willing to join it because it has opportunities at the end of the course. 

In the campus recruitments, we have always found very many employers coming in or people with international brands coming in and also giving them the opportunity for high-end jobs straightaway. No wonder even as we heard a few words of criticism while some are happy that all of you have spoken and supported the Bill. Here and there, we did hear concerns expressed by some of the hon. Members asking why is it so expensive, is it really dealing with leather, is this really going to be rural based, are we going to draw students from the rural areas and if you are drawing students from rural areas, how can you price yourself so high. These are the voices which we have heard. 

The course is, when I said, self-financed, I mean this. I am not saying that the capital expenditure for building the institutes will be taken from the students, not at all. It is the fee which is going to be the course’s fee which is going to be taken from the students and in that, it is fully self-financing. Since the nature of the course has been such and the job opportunities have been so very well knit, the cost of the course has never deterred students from coming and joining, and that itself proves that today, many of the States which want these centres to be present, which the last of the hon. Members who spoke, wanted it in Kozhikode. There are many other States which have asked for it. I know the Chief Minister of Jharkhand and I fully support his thought. He has been repeatedly asking that for a State like Jharkhand, to give an FDDI would make sense. We have friends from Mumbai who have spoken. Hon. Members who have raised the voice as to how Dharavi on its own has brought in that specialism of cottage-based nature of work, but also providing high-class leather goods, thereby earning a lot of foreign exchange. So, this sector has had a lot of emotional connect. 

We had Kumari Anju Bala, hon. Member of Kanpur, so vividly narrating her experience, when she had gone even as a young Member handling her household and also running the shop for her father. This is a sector in which a lot of Indians can directly relate.

You also heard our Kataria Ji speaking about himself and he spoke with a sense of honour and respect on how he has learnt the skill himself from his aged father, but not very many have been fortunate to learn it from anybody for that matter, leave alone their fathers. The setting up of the Institute, therefore, was not to lose out on a skill which will touch upon the lives of so many people, who desperately need modern ways of making footwear. 

I earnestly heard the Member, Shri Vishweshwar Reddy talk about going to his village and try to make the mochi do his chappals which he is wearing, which has a recycled tyre in it and how that has also got to be promoted. He also said equally that today the market for such things is dying and today the market is for branded footwear which comes with a designer label. We have heard several Members also say that if you have a high design in Puducherry, it still does not occupy the same level of market globally. Global brands dominate and there is no Indian brand as yet in it. 

But if we do not give that kind of a modern skill, that skill which is very much linked with tastes and fashion, we are not going to be able to have the manpower which can, on its own, either using Mudra loans or by associating themselves with good brand providers can provide that kind of a skill and technology to capture the global market for which India has, in every way, the advantages, be it the leather which is available; be it the tanning industry which, over the centuries, has done a lot of good work. 

I heard one of the hon. Members talk about how local tanning things like natural residues have been used in India and that has spread all over the country and as a result, today India’s tanning techniques are considered to be very good. Hon. Deputy Speaker, Sir, you are from Tamil Nadu. Ttile: Further discussion on Sustainable Development Goals - "way forward for the health and well being for all", raised by Shri Anurag Singh Thakur on the 30th March, 2017 (Discussion not concluded).

HON. DEPUTY SPEAKER: Now we will take up item no. 16- Discussion on Sustainable Development Goals under Rule 193.

श्रीमती भावना गवली (पाटील)(यवतमाल-वाशिम) : उपाध्यक्ष महोदय, आपने मुझे बोलने का मौका दिया है, इसके लिए मैं आपका धन्यवाद करती हूँ। एसडीजी पर हम चर्चा कर रहे हैं, जो चर्चा अनुराग जी ने शुरू की थी। स्वास्थ्य संबंधी चर्चा हम कर रहे हैं। हमारी अध्यक्ष महोदया ने हर सत्र में एक विऐाय ले कर उस पर चर्चा करने की बात कही है। आज स्वास्थ्य के वि­ऐाय में देखा जाए तो एसडीजी में भारत का स्थान 188 में से 143 है। यह हमारे लिए एक गंभीर बात है। 

16.31 hours (Shri Pralhad Joshi in the Chair) 

आज भारत में स्वास्थ्य के ऊपर जो खर्चा होता है, उसमें 184 देशों में से 178वें स्थान पर हमारा देश है। निम्न आय वाले जो देश हैं जैसे - बंगलादेश, नेपाल, श्रीलंका आदि इन देशों से भी हम पीछे हैं। आज अपनी जीडीपी का तीन प्रतिशत स्वास्थ्य के ऊपर चाइना खर्च करता है। अमरीका में जीडीपी का 8.3 प्रतिशत खर्च होता है, जबकि ब्रिटेन 9.6 प्रतिशत पर पहुंचा है। विश्व स्वास्थ्य संगठन का भी यह कहना है कि जीडीपी की पांच प्रतिशत राशि स्वास्थ्य के ऊपर खर्च की जाए, लेकिन आज हमारे देश में जीडीपी का 1.2 प्रतिशत ही खर्च होता है। यह गंभीर बात है। 

सभापति महोदय, हम नई स्वास्थ्य नीति लाने जा रहे हैं। कैबिनेट ने भी उसे मंजूरी दी है। दोनों सदनों में भी यह विधेयक पेश किया गया है। सन् 2002 में इस नीति को बनाया गया था और सन् 2016 में फिर से इस नीति को लाया गया है। मैं कहना चाहती हूँ कि जैसे हमारा भारत देश बहुत बड़ा देश है, बहुत ज्यादा जनसंख्या हमारे देश में है, उसकी स्वास्थ्य जरूरतों को पूरा करने के लिए सरकार के पास जो भी सुविधाएंं हैं, वे कम हैं। क्या उसे देखते हुए निजी क्षेत्र में पीपीपी मोड से हम हॉस्पिटल्स बनाने जा रहे हैं? मुझे लगता है कि ऐसा करने की आवश्यकता है। जैसे दिल्ली के एम्स में पीपीपी मोड पर अस्पताल चलाए जाते हैं, उसी तरह से चंडीगढ़ में भी पीपीपी मोड पर एक सरकारी अस्पताल चलाया जाता है और उनकी रिपोर्ट समाधानकारक है।

दूसरा ज्वांट वेंचर, राजीव गांधी सुपर स्पेशिलिटी हॉस्पिटल बैंगलोर है। अपोलो के साथ टाइअप कर के राज्य सरकार उसे देख रही है। यह राज्य सरकार का प्रकल्प है। मुझे लगता है कि इसमें ज्वाइंट वेंचर भी करने की आवश्यकता है। 

इंफ्रास्ट्रक्चर और रोड में बीओटी का बहुत अच्छा रिजल्ट आया है तो क्या हम बीओटी पर भी जाना चाहेंगे? मोबाइल हैल्थ यूनिट की भी हमें बहुत आवश्यकता है। गांवों में जब हम जाते हैं तो गांवों में लोगों में हैल्थ के प्रति कोई जागरूकता नहीं है। बीपी होता है, शुगर होती है, ये छोटे-छोटे दिखने वाले रोग जरूर हैं, लेकिन उसके कारण स्वास्थ्य की बड़ी समस्या का निर्माण होता है तो मैं समझती हूँ कि मोबाइल हैल्थ यूनिट भी देने की आवश्यकता है और वह एनजीओ की तरफ से या निजी क्षेत्र से भी हो सकता है। मैं समझती हूँ कि यह नीति जो हम ला रहे हैं, इसमें चाइना ने अपनी जीडीपी का जितना पैसा खर्च किया है, उतना ही, तीन प्रतिशत पैसा खर्च करने की आवश्यकता हमें भी है। 

टेली मेडिसन को भी बढ़ावा देने की आवश्यकता है, ऐसा मैं समझती हूँ। जैसे हम देखते हैं कि जिला अस्पताल में हमें सुविधा तो मिलती है, लेकिन वहाँ स्वास्थ्य की पूरी सुविधा नहीं मिल पाती है। इसलिए जो शहरों में एम्स जैसे हॉस्पिटल हैं, जैसे मुम्बई में हम जे.जे. अस्पताल देखेंगे, टाटा हॉस्पिटल देखेंगे, वहाँ पर बड़ी संख्या में लोग स्वास्थ्य की सुविधा के लिए आते हैं। गाँव में उतनी सुविधाएँ नहीं हैं, डिस्ट्रिक्ट लेवल पर हॉस्पिटल में उतनी सुविधाएँ नहीं मिल पाती हैं। इसके लिए हमें टेली मेडिसन की भी आवश्यकता है, क्या उसे सरकार अपनी नीति में समावि­ऐट करने जा रही है? 

महोदय, प्राथमिक आरोग्य केद्र देखते हैं, उप-केद्र देखते हैं, आर.एच. है, डिस्ट्रिक्ट हॉस्पिटल्स हैं, जब हम प्राथमिक आरोग्य केद्र में जाते हैं तो वहाँ डॉक्टर्स उपलब्ध नहीं होते हैं। प्राथमिक आरोग्य केद्रों पर नर्सेज उपलब्ध नहीं होती हैं। कोई मेडिसिन वहाँ पर ठीक तरह से लोगों को मिलती नहीं है और मिलती है तो दो प्रकार की गोली देकर उनको भेज दिया जाता है या डिस्ट्रिक्ट हॉस्पिटल में उन्हें रेफर किया जाता है। मैं समझती हूँ कि यह बहुत चिन्ता का विऐाय है। मेरा एक सुझाव है कि अगर हम ब्लॉक लेवल पर, हमारा जो आर.एच. है, जो ग्रामीण रूग्णालय है, उसे पूरा फैसिलिटेट करके, अगर 40 किलोमीटर का वह ब्लॉक होता है या 60 किलोमीटर का वह ब्लॉक होता है, वहाँ से मरीज लाने के लिए एम्बुलेंस सेवा हम शुरू कर सकते हैं और उस एम्बुलेंस सेवा के माध्यम से ब्लॉक लेवल पर मरीज पहुँचेंगे और पूरी सुविधा उन्हें वहाँ ब्लॉक लेवल पर ही मिलेगी। उन्हें डिस्ट्रिक पर भी जाने की आवश्यकता नहीं पड़ेगी। 

दूसरी बात यह है कि हम 6-6 करोड़ रुपये देकर पीएचसी का निर्माण करते हैं, लेकिन वहाँ डॉक्टर्स न होने के कारण उस पीएचसी का कोई फायदा हमारे ग्रामीणों को होता हुआ नहीं दिख रहा है। डॉक्टर्स की संख्या की कमी है। हमारे यहाँ आज हम देखें तो 55 हजार एम.बी.बी.एस. सीट्स हैं और 25 हजार पी.जी. की सीट्स हैं। मैं समझती हूँ कि ये सीट्स पर्याप्त नहीं हैं। जैसे मेडिकल काउन्सिल है या डेन्टल काउन्सिल है, नर्सिंग काउन्सिल है, इनके माध्यम से निजी कॉलेजों को हम परमीशन देते हैं। 

महोदय, मैं कहना चाहूँगी कि ये जो काउन्सिल्स हैं, खासकर जो मेडिकल काउन्सिल है, उस पर गवर्नमेंट का कोई ज्यादा प्रभाव नहीं है या उनको ठीक तरह से चलाने के लिए जितना कन्ट्रोल होना चाहिए, मैं समझती हूँ कि उतना कन्ट्रोल सरकार का उनके ऊपर नहीं है। आज निजी कॉलेजों के माध्यम से भी बहुत अच्छी स्वास्थ्य की सुविधा मिल रही है। वे हमारे बच्चों को पढ़ाने का भी काम कर रहे हैं और वहाँ वे लोगों को हेल्थ की सुविधा भी दे रहे हैं। लेकिन एनआरआई का 15 परसेंट का कोटा निजी कॉलेजेज का बन्द करने का प्रयास सरकार के द्वारा हो रहा है या वह बन्द कर रही है। मैं यह भी यहाँ पर कहना चाहती हूँ कि उसे बन्द न किया जाये। 

महोदय, यहाँ पर जेनरिक औ­ऐाधि का उल्लेख किया गया है। इस साल में करीबन तीन हजार जेनरिक औ­ऐाधि स्टोर्स हम देने जा रहे हैं। यह बहुत बड़ा कदम सरकार ने लिया है। जेनरिक औऐाधि स्टोर्स में हमें बहुत कम दर पर कैन्सर, बी.पी. आदि सभी तरह की बीमारियों से सम्बन्धित दवाइयाँ मिलेंगी। इसकी वजह से गरीबों के लिए स्वास्थ्य सुविधा बहुत ही अच्छी और सस्ती दिखाई दे रही है। इसका लाभ बहुत सारी जगहों पर लिया जा रहा है। यह बहुत अच्छा कदम सरकार ने उठाया है। आयुऐा डिपार्टमेंट के बारे में मैं बोलना चाहूँगी कि यह पहले फैमिली वेलफेयर मंत्रालय के तहत आता था, उसे अलग करा दिया गया है। आयुर्वेद हमारी परम्परागत औऐाधि है, आयुर्वेद के माध्यम से अच्छा स्वास्थ्य बनाने की कोशिश करते हैं और यह परम्परागत है। इसलिए इसको भी बढ़ावा देने की आवश्यकता है। विशे­ऐाकर के योग को बढ़ावा देने का काम हमारे प्रधान मंत्री नरेद्र भाई मोदी जी ने खुद किया है। जब भी यहाँ पर जो भी योग के शिविर होते थे, उन शिविरों में वे खुद गये हैं। अगर हम आयुर्वेद का उपयोग करेंगे, योग का उपयोग करेंगे तो हमारे पास सालों-साल तक कोई बीमारी ही नहीं फटकेगी। इस प्रकार से इसका बहुत अच्छा उपयोग होने की आवश्यकता है। जैसा कि यहाँ पर बताया गया है कि वऐाऩ 2030 तक हम एसडीजी का गोल प्राप्त करने जा रहे हैं।

महोदय, मैं मंत्री जी से पूछना चाहती हूँ कि वऐाऩ 2030 तक हमें यह गोल पूरा करना है, लेकिन अगर हम अपनी बढ़ती हुई आबादी को नहीं रोक पाये तो वऐाऩ 2030 तक हम यह गोल कैसे पूरा कर पायेंगे? मुझे लगता है कि मंत्री जी सक्षम हैं, सरकार भी सक्षम है, जैसे नोटबंदी का निर्णय हमने लिया है, उसी प्रकार से मैं समझती हूँ कि जो लोक संख्या का कन्ट्रोल है, उसे भी बहुत अच्छे तरीके से हमारे देश के लिए शुरू करने की आवश्यकता है। 

सभापति जी, मैं मंत्री जी से यह कहना चाहती हूं, जैसे हर बारह मिनट में एक गर्भवती महिला की मौत हो रही है, क्योंकि उसे पूरी जो सुविधा होती है, वह नहीं मिल रही है, हर एक मिनट में पांच साल से कम उम्र के बच्चों की मौत हो रही है, इसलिए उनके लिए भी बहुत अच्छी सुविधाएंं देने की आवश्यकता है, ऐसा मैं समझती हूं। बाकी जो भी हमारी योजनाएंं चल रही हैं, जैसे पंतप्रधान स्वास्थ्य योजना, जननी सुरक्षा योजना इत्यादि बहुत अच्छे-से चल रही हैं। टी.बी. का प्रोग्राम देखिए, पल्स पोलियो प्रोग्राम को देखिए, आप देखिए कि पोलियो का कोई बच्चा आज हमें नज़र नहीं आता, इतनी अच्छी मुहिम छेड़ी गयी है। लेकिन, अगर हम अपनी शिक्षा व्यवस्था में बच्चों को ये सारी बातें बताएंं तो मुझे लगता है कि इसका उनके स्वास्थ्य के ऊपर बहुत अच्छा असर पड़ेगा, क्योंकि बच्चे बहुत जल्दी सीखते हैं। इसलिए इसमें स्वास्थ्य के ऊपर विशे­ऐा महत्व देने की आवश्यकता है। 

सभापति जी, मैं मंत्री जी का धन्यवाद करना चाहती हूं। मैं जिस क्षेत्र से आती हूं, वहां पर महाराऐट्र के यवतमाल क्षेत्र में गवर्नमेंट मेडिकल कॉलेज है और आपने 100 करोड़ रुपए वहां पर एक सुपर स्पेशियलिटी हॉस्पीटल के लिए दिए हैं। मेरे क्षेत्र के लोगों को बहुत अच्छी सुविधा देने का काम यहां पर सरकार ने और मंत्री जी ने किया है। मैं उनका बहुत-बहुत धन्यवाद करती हूं और मैं समझती हूं कि सारे गोल्स को निश्चित करने के लिए हमें और अच्छी तरह से प्लानिंग करने की आवश्यकता है। 

महोदय, आपने मुझे बोलने का मौका दिया, इसके लिए बहुत-बहुत धन्यवाद।

डॉ. संजय जायसवाल (पश्चिम चम्पारण) : धन्यवाद सभापति महोदय, आपने मुझे ‘एस.डी.जी. गोल - 3’ पर बोलने का मौका दिया। 

महोदय, सबसे पहले तो मैं अपनी माननीय लोकसभाध्यक्ष महोदया को बहुत-बहुत धन्यवाद देता हूं, क्योंकि तीन वऐााॉ में यह पहला डिस्कशन है, जिसे खुद उन्होंने इनिशिएट किया। यह बताता है कि हम स्वास्थ्य के प्रति कितने ज्यादा कमिटेड हैं, यह पूरी-की-पूरी संसद कितनी ज्यादा कमिटेड है। इतना ही नहीं, मैंने 17 फरवरी को हिन्दी दैनिक ‘अमर उजाला’ में उनका एक आर्टिकल पढ़ा था, जिसमें उन्होंने ‘सतत विकास लक्ष्य और भारत’ के नाम से जो लेख लिखा है, वह अपने आप में इतना कॉप्रीहैन्सिव है कि अगर उसे पढ़ा जाए तो हमें इसे कैसे एचीव करना है, इसके बारे में भी उसमें गाइडलाइंस माननीय लोकसभाध्यक्ष महोदया ने लिखी हैं। इसके अलावा, ‘अध्यक्षीय शोध कदम’ में उन्होंने जो सस्टेनेबेल डेवलपमेंट गोल्स के बारे में जो मीटिंग कराई थी, वह भी बहुत ही अच्छी थी। लेकिन, मैं आपके माध्यम से माननीय अध्यक्षा जी को एक बात कहना चाहता हूं कि जो स्पीकर्स इनिशिएटिव की मीटिंग है, उसे दस बजे किया जाए या एक बजे किया जाए, क्योंकि शाम को हमारे संसदीय कार्य मंत्री लोग… * कुछ ज्यादा हो गए हैं और हम लोगों को उस मीटिंग में बैठने का मौका नहीं मिल पाता है। इसीलिए, आज मैं यह अपॉर्च्यूनिटी लेता हूं कि स्पीकर्स इनिशिएटिव की मीटिंग का समय या तो आफ्टरनून में किया जाए या मॉर्निंग में किया जाए तो हम लोगों को भी बहुत सारी चीजों को सीखने का मौका मिलेगा। 

किसी भी देश की उन्नति के लिए तीन चीज़ों की सबसे ज्यादा आवश्यकता होती है। एक है, दृढ़ इच्छाशक्ति के साथ सक्षम नेतृत्व, दूसरा है अर्थ, और तीसरा है लक्ष्य। यह हमारा सौभाग्य है कि हमें आज माननीय प्रधान मंत्री श्री नरेद्र मोदी जी के तहत और माननीय श्री नड्डा जी के साथ काम करने का मौका मिला है और जिस दृढ़ इच्छाशक्ति के साथ, चाहे वह जी.एस.टी. हो, नोटबंदी हो, मेक-इन-इंडिया हो, स्टार्ट-अप इंडिया हो, मुद्रा योजना हो, इन सब चीज़ों के द्वारा जो देश के विकास पर ध्यान दिया गया है, वह अपने आप में एक ऐतिहासिक कदम है। 

इसके साथ ही, मैं माननीय नड्डा जी के प्रति बहुत ही आभारी हूं कि हमारी जी.डी.पी. में हेल्थ का जो शेयर है, उसे 1.5 परसेंट से बढ़ाकर 2.5 परसेंट करने का उन्होंने लक्ष्य रखा है। वैसे तो हमारी यू.पी.ए. सरकार ने भी वऐाऩ 2005 में लक्ष्य रखा था कि हम वऐाऩ 2012 तक जी.डी.पी. में इसे 2.5औ करेंगे। लेकिन, कुछ नहीं हुआ और हम 1.15 परसेंट से हम 0.1 परसेंट भी आगे नहीं बढ़ सके। लेकिन, मुझे पूरा विश्वास है कि हमारे माननीय प्रधान मंत्री जी के नेतृत्व में स्वास्थ्य मंत्रालय जी.डी.पी. का 2.5औ खर्च करेगा, क्योंकि पैसे खर्च करने पर भी योजनाएंं सफल न हों, यह हो सकता है, लेकिन बिना पैसे के योजनाएंं सफल हो जाएंं, यह नहीं हो सकता। इसीलिए, मैं बहुत आभारी हूं कि सस्टेनेबल डेवलपमेंट गोल्स को एचीव करने के लिए 2.5औ का जो लक्ष्य रखा गया है, वह बहुत ही अच्छा है। 

मैं माननीय मंत्री जी को बहुत‑बहुत धन्यवाद देता हूं, आज तक स्वास्थ्य विभाग का केवल एक ही मतलब था कि कितने अस्पताल खुले हैं, दवाइयों पर कितने पैसे मिले, इसके अलावा स्वास्थ्य के मामले में और कोई बात ही नहीं चलती थी। एस.डी.जी. अचीव करना है तो केवल दवाई तथा अस्पताल से ही अचीव नहीं कर सकते हैं। हमारे यहां पंद्रह सालों के बाद नेशनल हेल्थ पॉलिसी आई है और इसमें सबसे ज्यादा ध्यान स्वस्थ नागरिक अभियान को दिया गया है, न कि स्वास्थ्य मंत्रालय द्वारा दिए गए पैसे को दिया गया है। यह पूरा का पूरा एक कंप्रिहेंसिव लिट्रेचर है, जिसमें पूरा ध्यान स्वस्थ नागरिक अभियान पर दिया गया है। स्वास्थ्य के क्षेत्र में जो पूरे सात प्वाइंट्स दिए गए हैं, उनमें सबसे पहला प्वाइंट स्वच्छ भारत अभियान है। 

जब तक हम भारत को खुले में शौच से मुक्त नहीं कर पाएंंगे, जनता को स्वच्छ पानी नहीं दे पाएंंगे, प्रदूऐाण मुक्त एनवायरमेंट नहीं दे पाएंंगे, तब तक स्वास्थ्य पर करोड़ों रूपये खर्च करने के बावजूद भी हमें कोई लाभ नहीं होने जा रहा है। मैं माननीय प्रधान मंत्री जी का बहुत आभारी हूं कि उन्होंने घरेलू प्रदऐाण के लिए प्रधान मंत्री उज्ज्वला योजना हो, चाहे वह नदियों की सफाई के लिए ‘नमामि गंगे‘ योजना हो, चाहे स्मार्ट सिटी योजना हो, विगत दस सालों से जो कैंपा फंड यूज नहीं हो रहा था, चाहे उसका सही से उपयोग होना हो, कोयले पर चार सौ टन से अधिक पर सेस का उपयोग रिन्यूएबल एनर्जी के लिए किया जाएगा, ये सारी चीजें कंप्रिहेंसिव हेल्थ केयर की तरफ इंडीकेट करती है। हमारी सरकार का यह प्रयास बताती है कि प्रत्येक नागरिक के स्वास्थ्य के हर क्षेत्र के प्रति कितनी ज्यादा डिटरमाइंड है। हम व्यक्ति के स्वास्थ्य के प्रत्येक क्षेत्र पर ध्यान देंगे और एक स्वस्थ भारत का निर्माण करेंगे। इस देश की 6.30 करोड़ आबादी प्रत्येक साल ए.पी.एल. से बी.पी.एल. फैमिली हो जाती हैं और इसका कारण केवल उनका हेल्थ का बजट है। 

आज तक जितने भी मूल्य वृद्धि सूचकांक हैं, उसमें अगर किसी भी चीज का पैसा बढ़ जाता है तो हम सब लोग महंगाई की बात करने लग जाते हैं और कहने लगते हैं कि बहुत महंगाई बढ़ गई है। इस पर प्रत्येक साल सदन में चर्चा भी होती है, लेकिन इस देश के सवा छह करोड़ व्यक्ति जो प्रत्येक साल ए.पी.एल से बी.पी.एल परिवार में चले जाते हैं, हम लोग उनका थोक मूल्य सूचकांक से कोई रिलेशनशिप ही नहीं रखते हैं, इसके बारे में भी हम लोगों को सोचने की जरूरत है कि दवाइयों की भी एम.आर.पी. फिक्स होनी चाहिए।

आज मैं माननीय मंत्री जी से अनुरोध करूंगा कि दवाइयों का भी एम.आर.पी. फिक्स किया जाए। जब हम साबुन, तेल, चावल तथा दाल आदि वस्तुओं का एम.आर.पी. फिक्स करते हैं तो दवाइयों पर एम.आर.पी. क्यों नहीं फिक्स होती है। इसके अलावा, मैं आभारी हूं कि इस कार्यक्रम में संतुलित भोजन तथा नियमित व्यायाम की व्यवस्था भी रखी गई है। इसके लिए आई.सी.डी.एस. के तहत महिलाओं को स्पलीमेंट्री न्यूट्रीशन तथा सबला कार्यक्रम आदि जैसी बहुत सारी चीजों का लक्ष्य रखा गया है।

मैं बधाई देना चाहूंगा कि जो सस्टेनेब्ल डेवलपमेंट गोल है, उसको अचीव करने के लिए कालाजार, टी.बी., लैप्रोसी जैसी बीमारियों को समयबद्ध खत्म करने की बात की जा रही है, जो नॉन‑कम्युनिकेवल डिजिजेज़ हैं, उनमें प्री‑मैच्योरड डेथ आज के मुकाबले 25 प्रतिशत कम हो जाएंं, इसका भी लक्ष्य भारत सरकार ने रखा है। इसी तरह से आज एक हजार की आबादी पर एक बिस्तर भी उपलब्ध नहीं है, उसको बढ़ाकर दो बिस्तर प्रति एक हजार की आबादी के लिए रखा गया है। वऐाऩ 2025 तक पी.एच.सी. को 50 पर्सेंट से ज्यादा बढ़ाने का लक्ष्य रखा गया है, पाँच वऐाऩ के बच्चों की मृत्यु दर 23 है। हमारी सरकार इन सब पर बहुत ही जबरदस्त तरीके से काम कर रही है। मैंने खुद देखा है कि मिशन इंद्रधनु­ऐा के तहत बच्चों की जान बचाने का काम माननीय स्वास्थ्य मंत्री जी ने किया है, वह बहुत ही ऐतिहासिक है। मेरे जिले में 35 पर्सेंट बच्चों का ही इम्युनाइजेशन होता था, लेकिन आज वह 63 पर्सेंट हो गया है। यह केवल मिशन इंद्रधनु­ऐा का ही देन है। इस तरह के कन्संट्रेटेड वर्क करने से ही हमें लाभ मिलेगा। मैं मंत्री जी का आभार प्रकट करना चाहूंगा कि अभी नए प्रोजेक्ट में पेंटावैलेंट वैक्सिन तो लिया ही है, अब वे पी.सी.वी. वैक्सीन भी इंट्रोडय़ूस कर रहे हैं। यह पहली बार है कि कोई पायलट प्रोजेक्ट बिहार, उत्तर प्रदेश तथा हिमाचल प्रदेश में होने जा रहा है। आज तक यह मानसिकता थी कि कोई भी नया पायलट प्रोजेक्ट शुरू करना होता था तो वह कर्नाटक, केरल तथा तमिलनाडु में कर दिया जाता था, जहां सारा इंफ्रास्ट्रक्चर तैयार है, कहीं कुछ करने की जरूरत नहीं है, आपको केवल वैक्सीन इंट्रोडय़ूस कर देना है और सारा काम खत्म हो गया। कोई भी नयी चीज बिहार, उत्तर प्रदेश तथा हिमाचल प्रदेश के डिफीकल्ट टेरेन्स में इंट्रोडय़ूस करना अपने आप में इस सरकार की क्षमता बताती है कि वह कितनी डिटरमाइंड है।

एक पी.सी.वी.वैक्सीन प्राइवेट क्षेत्र में एक बच्चों के लिए दस हजार रूपये से भी ज्यादा की कॉस्ट पड़ती है। इन्होंने इस चीज को यूनिवर्सल इम्यूनाइजेशन प्रोग्राम के तहत एक पायलट प्रोजेक्ट के रूप में दिया है। इसके लिए मैं बहुत‑बहुत बधाई देता हूं कि आज देश में प्रतिवऐाऩ पौने दो लाख बच्चे तो केवल निमोनिया से मरते हैं। इन दोनों के इंट्रोडक्शन से बहुत ही फायदा होगा। मैं माननीय स्वास्थ्य मंत्री जी के दो मानकों से संतु­ऐट नहीं हूं। एक, जीवन प्रत्याशा जो 67 से 70 वऐाऩ रखी है, यह लक्ष्य अगर 2014 में रखते, तब तो अच्छा लगता, क्योंकि उस समय जिस ढंग से स्वास्थ्य सेवा चल रही थी, आज स्वास्थ्य मंत्री जी ने पूरे स्वास्थ्य विभाग को जिस ढर्रे पर ला दिया है, यह तो अपने आप ही 70 वऐाऩ पहुंच जाएगी। अगर लक्ष्य रखना है, तो इस देश को बढ़ाने के लिए एक एंंबिशियस लक्ष्य होना चाहिए, जिसकी मैं मंत्री जी से उम्मीद करता हूं। ...(व्यवधान) यह कम से कम 73 हो, जो कि श्रीलंका का है। मैं कोई अमेरिका और इंग्लैंड की बात नहीं कर रहा हूं।

इसी प्रकार से हमारा 2.1 टीएफआर है। पॉपुलेशन स्थिरीकरण के लिए 2.1 प्रति परिवार टीएफआर का लक्ष्य है। मैं इससे भी संतु­ऐट नहीं हूं। पूरे के पूरे एसडीजी गोल्स अगर एचीव करने हैं, तो जैसा कि भावना जी ने कहा कि बिना जनसंख्या नियंत्रण किए हुए हम लोग किसी भी काम में सफल नहीं हो सकते हैं। जो पॉलिसी डाक्यूमेंट है, उसमें मैंने देखा पॉपुलेशन स्टैब्लाइजेशन में केवल पांच लाइनें लिखी हुई हैं और एक ही साफ लक्ष्य रखा गया है कि नसबंदी को 5 पर्सेंट से 30 पर्सेंट करना है। मेरा माननीय स्वास्थ्य मंत्री जी से अनुरोध होगा कि हमें च्वॉइस का बास्केट बढ़ाना होगा। आज मलेशिया जैसा देश 1.9 पर खड़ा है। हम बांग्लादेश से भी पीछे हैं। न जाने क्यों, संसद हो, चाहे बाहर हो, हम जनसंख्या स्थिरीकरण के बारे में साफ-साफ बात नहीं करना चाहते हैं। ...(व्यवधान) पढ़े-लिखे लोगों के बच्चे कम हो रहे हैं, यह जाहिर बात है। मैं किसी को दो­ऐा नहीं दे रहा हूं, लेकिन यह बहाना नहीं चलेगा, क्योंकि बांग्लादेश हर तरह से हम लोगों से पीछे है, फिर भी वहां जनसंख्या स्थिरीकरण एचीव कर ली गई है। वहां पर जुमे की नमाज के बाद मौलाना बोलता है कि दो बच्चे से ज्यादा मत पैदा करो। हमारे यहां क्या परम्परा है। हमारे यहां यह हो रहा है कि ज्यादा बच्चे पैदा करो, कोई और बोलता है कि वे 6 बच्चे पैदा कर रहे हैं, तुम 8 बच्चे पैदा करो। क्या इससे देश चलेगा? हमें इस बात पर बहुत सीरियस बहस करनी होगी। मैं आज मंत्री जी से अनुरोध करूंगा कि हर धर्म के गुरुओं को बुलाकर इसके बारे में भी बात करें। इस देश की भलाई के लिए हर रिलीजन के लोगों को समझाना होगा। अगर मंत्री जी चाहें, तो मैं अपने लोक सभा क्षेत्र में, यह गांधी जी का सत्याग्रह का सौ साल है, मैं इनीशिएटिव ले सकता हूं, मैं अपने यहां सभी धर्म गुरुओं को बुलाकर इस बारे में बात कर सकता हूं, क्योंकि पूरी की पूरी जनसंख्या की स्थिति बिगड़ रही है। आज 24 प्रदेश अपना लक्ष्य एचीव कर चुके हैं। जो तथाकथित बीमार राज्य हैं, बिहार, उत्तर प्रदेश, मध्य प्रदेश, राजस्थान, इसमें हम लोग बहुत पीछे हैं। पूरे देश की आबादी 352 व्यक्ति प्रति किलोमीटर है, बिहार 1,180 पर है और उसके बाद हम 3.3 के हिसाब से भागे जा रहे हैं। हमारी संस्कृति की नीति है, सर्व धर्म समभाव, लेकिन आज क्या हो रहा है? पारसियों की संख्या घटती जा रही है, जैनियों की संख्या घटती जा रही है, तो अगर हम 2.1 एचीव भी कर लिए और समाज के सभी तबकों को एक बराबर हिस्सेदारी नहीं मिली तो यह सफीशिएंंट नहीं है। मैं इसलिए आपसे अनुरोध करूंगा कि बिहार को, यूपी को, मध्य प्रदेश को, राजस्थान को जैसे इन्होंने मिशन इंद्रधनु­ऐा के तहत स्पेशल पैकेज इम्युनाइजेशन के लिए दिया, उसी तरह से जनसंख्या नियंत्रण पर भी जो राज्य पीछे छूटे हुए हैं, उन पर एक्शन लें। उन राज्यों के लिए अलग से व्यवस्था हो। 

आज बच्चे पैदा करने पर हम 6 हजार रुपये दे रहे हैं, लेकिन नहीं करने पर उसको 5 सौ रुपये मिलते हैं। हमें पूरी की पूरी प्रोत्साहन नीति बदलनी पड़ेगी। अगर कोई एक बच्चा पैदा करता है, तो उसके लिए यह घाटे का सौदा है, क्योंकि उसको आज पीडीएस से 15 किलो अनाज मिलेगा और जिसके दस बच्चे हैं, उसको 60 किलो मिलेगा। हम नहीं कहते हैं कि इसमें कोई कड़ा कानून बनाया जाए, पर जो एक बच्चा पैदा कर रहा है, उसको तो इंसेंटिव दीजिए। 

आज शिक्षा में नीति है कि 25 बच्चों को हम प्राइवेट स्कूलों में फ्री एजुकेश्न देंगे। हम यह क्यों नहीं करते कि जिसका एक बच्चा है, उसको सबसे पहले उस 25 प्रतिशत शिक्षा वाले स्कूल में हिस्सा मिलेगा, क्यों नहीं हम करते कि हम 35 किलो अनाज देंगे, तुम्हारे 2 बच्चे हों या 10 बच्चे हों, यह तुझ समझो। 

सबसे ज्यादा बच्चे पैदा होने का क्या कारण है? लोगों को डर लगता है कि मेरा बच्चा मर गया तो क्या होगा। ...(व्यवधान) यह सही बात है, गांव में यही स्थिति है। जो एक बच्चा पैदा करे, क्यों नहीं हम शुरू से उसको इंश्योरेंस दें। आप आरएसवीवाई करते हैं, अन्य दूसरी योजनायें करते हैं, कितनी सरकारी सब्सिडी बचाता है, अगर वह एक या दो बच्चे पैदा करता है। उसके तहत मैं अनुरोध करूंगा कि जो लोग एक बच्चा पैदा करते हैं, उन्हें भी इस तरह की नीतियों में लेना चाहिए।...(व्यवधान) बहुत सारे प्रदेशों ने दो बच्चों का कानून पंचायती राज में लागू किया है। उससे कोई नुकसान नहीं हुआ। मेरे प्रदेश बिहार में सन् 2008 में कानून लागू हुआ कि नगरपालिका में कोई दो बच्चों से ज्यादा पैदा नहीं करेगा। उसका नतीजा हुआ कि वऐाऩ 2010 के चुनाव में बिहार के हर शहर में एनडीए का विधायक बना था। यह कहना कि जनसंख्या की बात करने या नियम बनाने से कोई दिक्कत होगी, सही बात नहीं है। मैं कहूंगा कि माननीय मंत्री जी जनसंख्या के बारे में जरूर विचार करें।

SHRI GAURAV GOGOI (KALIABOR): Sir, I thank you very much for giving me this opportunity to speak on this very important subject.

There was a time when health care was not available in remote parts of India primarily because of poor connectivity, lack of roads and not enough funds for creating hospitals. If people wanted good quality health care, they would have to walk for kilometres and travel for days in order to reach even a place where there was a doctor. But a lot changed when in the previous decade the Government of India launched the National Health Mission and the National Rural Health Mission. A lot of funds were pumped in through the National Rural Health Mission. What did this achieve? It made health care accessible to large parts of India’s population. Because of the funds made available through the National Rural Health Mission, hospitals, sub-centres and Primary Health Care Centres were created in those villages and areas in which they had never seen a hospital before. So, one of the major achievements that our policy did was creating the health infrastructure. 

Now, having built the hardware of hospitals, Primary Health Centres, etc. we must focus on the quality issue, the quality of health care. Often what is happening is that because of too many patients lining up outside the clinics, doctors are in a rush to prescribe antibiotics. Within two minutes, without making a proper diagnosis, the doctors say, “you have headache, here is the antibiotic”. As a result of which what is happening is that the common infection, like the common viral, viral fever, viral cold, etc. are developing this huge resistance to antibiotic. Now, we have this phenomenon of superbugs. This is exceptionally dangerous. The same happens in agriculture. When we use too much of pesticides in the fields, the pests develop resistance to these pesticides and it takes that much more pesticides to kill the same pest. 

The same thing is happening in the human system. Superbugs, these days, are becoming more and more dangerous. There is even a term called ‘New Delhi -- NDM’ which is creating a bad image in the world health community. So, I urge the Ministry of Health to look at this issue of superbugs. Train the doctors and facilitate these doctors. This is becoming a huge risk that even a common cold can become fatal. But is the Government doing enough? Is the Government serious? 

I remember reading a Press headline. When the ease of doing business ranking of India just improved by one – you know the ease of doing business ranking is a huge priority for this priority – the PMO was so concerned that they organised a Cabinet meeting, wrote letters and gave instructions to Chief Secretaries of all the States. 

There is another ranking. It is called the Global Hunger Index. In that the ranking of India fell from 83 to 97. It fell by almost by 14 spots. But was there a similar meeting? Was a Cabinet meeting called? We have heard this statistics on malnutrition. Around 50 per cent of India’s children are vulnerable to malnutrition. Has there ever been a Cabinet meeting? The Government pays so much attention to the ease of doing business, but completely forgets about hunger and malnutrition.

Has there been a Cabinet meeting? Not a beep, not a word, not an instruction from this Government which claims that health is a priority for them. 

There is one example to which I want to draw the attention of the House. It is the way the UPA Government eradicated polio from our country. Polio was a debilitating disease. The way we eradicated polio is a lesson in health care. There was door to door movement of ASHA workers, there was door to door movement of community health workers. Polio drops were administered on a specific time schedule. The entire population of India had to be trained on this particular schedule. The Government flooded the public health advertisements. That is the way we should do it. We need a movement if we really want to improve the health scenario. A discussion in the Parliament is very good. But if there is a lesson to be learnt there needs to be a healthcare movement like the way we did earlier when it came to eradication of polio.

You must be having the same problem. When the children of poor families go to Anganwadi centres, the money that gets released for their food should be such that there should be enough money in one Anganwadi centre to buy 100 days of food. But what is happening? For example, in my constituency, they have money only to buy food for 58 days. These are the most deprived families, these are the most deprived communities. Why is there such a delay in the release of the Central funds?  Why is there no better coordination between the Centre and States so that Anganwadi workers not only have enough money to buy 100 days of food but have a surplus so that they are not so dependent upon the Centre?

Sir, I want to talk about malnutrition. The World Bank Report says that malnutrition is a silent emergency. We must wake up to this problem. As a result of that, they are falling sick, they are not paying attention in school, they are dropping out and their attendance is suffering. I know various State Governments are doing a lot. Maharashtra is doing a lot, Tamil Nadu is doing a lot, in Assam, and in my constituency also we are trying to do a lot. There are many other States that are doing very well in this regard. So we must try to collect a database as to what are the best practices that are being followed across the States.

17.11 hours (Dr. Ratna De (Nag) in the Chair) 

For example, in my State, we have come up with a Nutrition Toolkit, a toolkit which helps teachers explain best nutritional practices to children. It is very simple. In the same way as we are using teachers to help educate children about hand washing, we can work with teachers to help educate parents and their children about better nutritional practices. One of the simplest things is to eat green leafy vegetables which are indigenous, which do not have to be bought from a distant market, but which are locally grown and locally procured.

In my constituency, what we are doing is, we are helping children in schools to develop School Nutrition Gardens through creating Organic Farming Clubs. The children are being taught as to how to grow green leafy local varieties of vegetable on their school playground. When they produce such vegetables, they are selling that to the Mid-Day Meal authorities because they have to procure these vegetables and then, these vegetables are being consumed by children as part of their Mid-Day Meal Programme. It is a huge success. Children are learning the basics of organic farming, of healthy eating practices, they are able to identify as to which are the local varieties of vegetables and by selling them to the local Mid-Day Meal authorities, whatever money they earn, they put it in their own individual account. What we have done is, for each student, we have opened a Minor Savings Account. So, when a child grows vegetables and sells them to the local Mid-Day Meal authorities, the money that the child earns does not go to the parent or to the headmaster, but it goes to his own Minor Savings Account. So, from a very young age of 13 or 14 years, a child is learning the basics of agricultural entrepreneurship. This is a very interesting model. A lot of States are experimenting with this School Nutrition Gardens. The UNICEF is working on this in Delhi as well. I urge upon the Health Ministry to look at this concept. It requires a synergy between the Ministries of Women and Child Development, Health and Family Welfare, Education and Agriculture. But this is the way we need to work. We have to work in a series of convergence.

I have gone through the summary of the New National Health Policy. It is difficult for me to understand as to what is the priority of this Government, what is the one theme that this Government is going to focus on. For instance, in education it is very clear. So, through SSA, Mid-Day Meal Programme, the focus of previous Governments was to make education accessible to a large population. Now, over the last couple of years, now that schools have been set up, the focus is on quality of education, learning outcomes, making sure the students are able to understand what is being taught in classroom. But when I look at the Draft National Health Policy, it seems to be a hash of what already exists. What is the core thrust area? It talks about setting various targets, but does not give a clear road map. So, I want the New National Health Policy to give a clear thrust area and tell us as to how we are going to measure this.

Madam, I think that we need right now is a new idea towards healthcare. We have talked a lot about it. I do not think we should blame anyone. We should not blame the doctors, nurses etc. Our people do not have enough awareness. What we really need right now is political leadership. If the Chief Minister of every State, if every MP, MLA, not just the Health Minister, but the PMO and the Prime Minister himself makes healthcare a priority, gives it the requisite funds and say that we are going to focus on the quality of healthcare, that is how we are going to achieve our SDGS. It is good to have this discussion, it sensitizes us, but we have to back to the field and, through this discussion, I do hope that MMR, the way it has increased in Gujarat gets reviewed. We must take lessons from the eradication of polio that was done under the UPA regime and we must come out with more funds for the National Rural Health Mission but not with decreased funds.

When the basic reason for Tuberculosis is poverty and when the treatment of it is removal of poverty itself, then how is it possible? That is one paradox.

Then, there is another paradox – Scabies. It mostly affects the people who live in an overcrowded place with unhygienic conditions and unhygienic food habits, particularly slum areas. किसी को स्केबीज़ होने पर हम उसे सलाह देते हैं कि वह उस जगह पर दवा लगाए, रोज साबुन लगाकर नहाए, साफ कपड़े पहने, साफ बेड पर सोए और हर दिन बेड-शीट चेंज करे आदि। हम उसे यह सलाह देते हैं, परंतु वह हँसता रहता है और हमारी सलाह नहीं मानता है। वह हमसे यह पूछ सकता है कि यदि उसके पास ये सारी सुविधाएँ होतीं, तो वह बीमार ही क्यों होता। So, this is the paradox. While dealing with the health issues, certain paradoxes will come across. Directly dealing with health means removing the diseases from human beings, which is not the issue. There are many interrelated things. For example, let us take modern epidemic. You can call it pandemic. Diabetes mellitus is a pandemic. Every third or fourth person in Asia, especially in India is suffering from it. 

Then, the phenotype of Indian physical personality is spindle shaped, which has automatically developed in 40 to 50 years’ span. The longer is the waist length the shorter the life span. Wherever the waist length of the people is large, they are particularly prone to Diabetes Mellitus. The fat deposits in the central abdomen and causes Diabetes. At the moment, every third or fourth person in India is prone to Diabetes. 

Let us see what the treatment for Diabetes is. We have to do exercise everyday; we have to change our lifestyle and we have to change our food habits. But what happens? Of late, the computers have come. The economy is developing. The families are becoming nuclear. We are moving towards fast foods like pizzas, burgers, pastas, etc. They are all readymade foods. These are all junk foods. जंक फूड में फैट होता है। Fat will lead to Diabetes Mellitus. The people will be sedentary and they like to be sitting in the chair looking at their laptops doing nothing else. Their parents also do not look after them. So, it is because of such type of occupations that certain diseases have come into our life. 

In Indian context, where people are not prone to these diseases and disorders, of late we are acquiring these disorders. There are other disorders like hypertension, diabetes, hyperlipidemia – which means a lot of cholesterol in the blood – and sudden cardiac arrest. In Indian medical history, females getting heart attack was very uncommon. We never came across any myocardial dysfunction or heart attack in females till recently, till the year 2000. Of late, with the introduction of modern-day living, computers, so-called junk food and sedentary lifestyle without any exercise, even females are also undergoing massive heart attacks and dying in the hospitals. Therefore, lifestyle is also linked to health. There are many factors linked with health – geographical location, economic condition, lifestyle etc – which are inter-related. In view of this, taking health per se as a single thing or a single goal may not be successful. 

I would like to request the hon. Minister that our approach towards health should always be integrated. Therefore, let us not consider health just as free from disorder; health means physical well-being, psychological well-being; and above all, spiritual well-being. Then only, the country will be better off. 

When the citizens of our country are happy, our country will be a happy country and our Happiness Index will also be very high. That is how health has to be viewed always. I urge upon the concerned authorities to have an integrated approach to have better health of the citizens and the youth of the country. They should also look at changing the lifestyles of people because there are many things which are coming up as occupational hazards due to occupational environment and practices. 

Jai Hind, Jai Telugu Desam. 

SHRI JITENDRA CHAUDHURY (TRIPURA EAST): Sir, vanakam. I thank you for giving me this opportunity to speak. 

I would like to thank my friend, Shri Anurag Thakur, for initiating the discussion on this issue of Sustainable Development Goal and also the hon. Speaker, Madam, for her indulgence so that this issue can be discussed threadbare and participated in by Members from all quarters. 

Here, we have been discussing about the health. While most of our learned Members were participating, almost everyone was saying that there should be more AIIMS-like hospitals and more super speciality hospitals. Of course, it is required, but what is the Sustainable Development Goal? It is not only health; there are many other aspects. The SDG has targeted 17 goals, 169 targets and 230 indicators. There is one health goal and within that goal are 13 targets and 26 indicators. 

Here, in this august House, particularly the physician and doctor Members have contributed a lot from the medical point of view, telling how different kind of diseases can be arrested or contained. Either it is health or other various kinds of social goals. Unless, in totality, our economy or social environment does not change, these goals cannot be achieved the way they are desired to be. 

If we see in our country today, what is the position in India? According to the Human Development Index, out of 194 countries, India’s position is 131. There are particularly some health related issues. 

Coming to tap water, I am not talking about safe or pure potable drinking water. Only 28 per cent of our countrymen have access to the tap water, both safe and unsafe. The next thing is sanitation. Of course, there is Swachh Bharat Mission. It is initiated not today; it was there even before also. Still, in our country, 47 per cent of our countrymen have access to sanitation. 

As regards nutrition, it is 38.7 per cent of our population. If we talk about children to whom we should provide not only nutrition but all the other favourable conditions also, it will be more. The female literacy rate was a very important segment of our society, but it is only 61.5 per cent. Longevity of life at birth is still 68.3 per cent, and 70 per cent of our women are suffering from anaemia. If we have to address these issues and achieve the goals, then yes, super-speciality hospitals, more AIIMS, more doctors, more paramedical are required, but there are certain other social parameters whose condition has to be changed. Unless it is ensured or achieved, whatever economic or health goals we set, it would be very difficult and cannot be achieved. 

Hence, I would like to suggest that as my previous speaker was telling that health means not only food and nutrition, but there are many other things involved in it. So, in our country, until and unless the public distribution system is made universal where each and every citizen of our country either poor or rich have access to food, the food security cannot be achieved and you cannot maintain the level of health and other parameters.

If we compare our country with China, then in many aspects China is far ahead of us. I am not talking about their political system and our political system, but it is true and we have to admit it. China has achieved their Independence two years after India. China’s population is more than what we have in our country, but though area-wise China is bigger than India, but China’s cultivable land is less than India. But, today, in terms of agriculture produce; in terms of industrial expansion; and in every aspect China is far ahead. Why is it so? I am not talking about the secondary or tertiary side. In the primary sectors like agriculture they have given that kind of access to the farmers; farmers means not just giving land, but together with all kind of conditions have been created that they get the seeds and all other things and their produce can be sold to the Government. 

In our country also, we are having much of the land and India has got a number of rivers, but that land reform of actually giving land to the tillers has not been given. Hence, the slogan of our freedom struggle that ‘give land to the tillers’ has not been achieved. 

Of course, as regards education, it is not only required to produce Graduates, Post Graduates, Doctorates, but impart education to build capacity of the human being / common citizen. So, universal education is not achieved. Of course, now, Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan and Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan are there, but still if we see in comparison to the other advancing countries as to how much we are really spending for education, it is very less. If we see our Budget, there are a number of such goals being declared, but the Budget for food security, agriculture, education, etc. are not being enhanced in that way. 

So, if we compare the economy in our country of these two-three years during 2014, the corporate media’s write-ups showed that one per cent rich of our Indian people in 2014 were owning 49 per cent of our total wealth. After two years, now, in 2016, it is 58.4 per cent, which means all the wealth is being accumulated in the hands of the very handful people. It is not being distributed that way. So, it is not to give any kind of expert’s views here but for self-retrospection, as to why this is happening, why India is lagging behind. Even we are far behind Sri Lanka and some other very poor countries in this aspect. So, this aspect should be taken care of. 

Today, on this Health Budget also, it is being said here that our public spending should be increased. How much should be our public spending? Two years ago, it was 1.15 per cent. This year, it is around 2.5 per cent. I think, not only the Health Budget, but the other sectors should also be taken care of. 

Here, I would like to cite another fact that under the initiative of the Speaker’s Office, there has been one Workshop recently. The Ex-Secretary of Health was giving the presentation. She mentioned as to what the disparities are between the countries and among the districts in our country. In the most backward district of Kerala, safe water access is 94 per cent. And in Bihar and U.P, in the most advanced districts, that is 98 and 96 per cent. The Most backward district of Kerala and the most advanced districts of Bihar and UP are almost the same. That is why, Kerala and your own State, Tamil Nadu, in terms of safe drinking water, nutrition and in other aspects are so advanced. Your most backward districts are highly advanced because they have a good social system and you have given importance for education, health, etc. and in other aspects also. That is why, today, it is coming up. So, until and unless this aspect is taken care of, just by increasing the number of AIIMS or having more doctors, nothing is going to be achieved. That is the participation on my part. I think, the Hon. Minister will take care of not only the setting up of the super-specialty hospital but also other conditions of the society. 

SHRIMATI SUPRIYA SULE (BARAMATI): I would actually like to thank the Speaker’s Office and the SRI Foundation, which is the Speaker’s researched initiative which had a detailed discussion last week with all the hon. MPs briefing them on SDGs and especially health. They had called all the hon. MPs. SRI has done a wonderful job to brief all of us on this health issue. 

Sir, the hon. Minister has been an exceptionally fine Minister. Even if I am in Opposition, I must compliment for all the achievements that he has got. He has been exceptionally supportive especially for our tobacco campaign. I am eternally grateful for him and I hope he sustains the support and makes sure that all the States also fight the challenges of tobacco control. I come from a tobacco-caused cancer surviving family. I really know the challenges that a family goes through when there is cancer in the family. It is a very difficult thing for a family to go through plus the cost of cancer and the availability of doctors is also an issue. 

I come from a State where probably India’s best doctors are available. I did mention to the hon. Minister and he was very considerate last time when I brought it up to him that Maharashtra has had some difficult issues regarding doctors. The health SDG can be achieved only if we have very fine doctors.

Unfortunately, in my State, we had a very bad incident about two weeks ago where an Orthopaedic doctor, who was asked to help relating to somebody’s brain haemorrhage issue and the doctor could not help or give proper healthcare. In an accident, one patient was brought to the hospital in Dhule District and he passed away. The doctor was attacked. The doctor kept telling them that it was not his specialisation, that he was an Orthopaedic doctor and that he was trying to do the best that he could. Unfortunately, the patient’s family got very emotional. They broke the hospital. They hurt the doctor. The doctor today is fighting for his life in the Dhule Hospital. He has had a haemorrhage; he has a broken skull and is on a respirator as we talk. 

The hon. Minister was very kind at that time saying that he would definitely address the issue of doctors’ security. I do not understand and respect the emotions of the family or the agony that the family went through. It was an exceptionally unfortunate incident. But I do not think it is really fair to beat up doctors. Then, all the doctors in Maharashtra went on strike. It was very unfortunate that the hon. Chief Minister of Maharashtra was not very kind to our doctors, and almost had to take action. It, unfortunately, Sir, turned very ugly. 

I think doctors do a great service in this country. They are the people who eventually will take us to this SDG which we all dream of. Technology makes a difference. Earlier speaker, Shri Jitendra Chaudhury talked about it; our Member from TDP talked about a lot of technology. India is changing. There are plenty of hospitals. The Government aspires to have an AIIMS everywhere. I also come from a District, which is Pune District, which has great public health centres also. We have a lot of good doctors; we have very good technology. But do we really have the technicians to run like a sonography machine? There are sonography machines all over, but can they really be used? Are our technicians trained for it? It is bought by the Government and it is sitting idle with dust on it, and that money is completely wasted. That is something about which we all really need to ponder over. 

Sir, I really come from an old school of thought. Technology is very good; it is definitely helping our lives get better. But at the same time, it is unfortunate that the concept of a family doctor does not exist any more. There was one time when you could walk into a doctor’s clinic and the old fashioned doctor would say, “This is wrong with you; just take this medicine and go away”, and there was really not such a big deal. But today, whenever you go, the clinical diagnosis is not something that really we see in the new generation doctors because technology has taken over. So, really, the cost of going to a doctor and the treatment has become so expensive that the minute you walk into a doctor’s clinic, it is like going into a court now. Every time you climb steps of a court, you are scared that you are stuck for 25 years. Unfortunately, if you go to a multi-specialist hospital anywhere in this country today, the bills are so scary that an average Indian today cannot afford even if he wants that service and doctors want to give it. So, it is a vicious circle that we are caught into. 

I will ask the hon. Minister that what we really need is a universal healthcare provision. How do we go forward with it? Is it about just reducing of costs or is insurance a big thing? That is something for this whole House to debate. Insurance, health and education are not issues that the House disagrees on at all. What are these? These are all programmes of continuity. Nobody is going to disagree on any health services. Nadda Ji, the hon. Minister, has come up with a very good immunisation programme, a vaccination programme in India. I would request him to add a very important vaccine which has come in India, which his office should probably go through it and see, is the cervical cancer vaccine, which is given to young girls. A lot of research has been done on it. Should we really add it to Mission Indradhanush or not is an optional thing; it is not compulsory. But we do see cervical cancer issues, especially amongst women. It is exceptionally high these days. A lot of people talked and even Jitendra Ji talked about anaemia; I think our Member from TDP talked about diabetes; and he also talked about hypertension. 

There was a time in India when India was not so advanced. There was a time we used to only have communicable diseases like Malaria, about which we had talked. But today the times have changed. We have managed to eradicate many of these communicable diseases. Today because of the lifestyle changes, we have non-communicable diseases like hypertension, diabetes, etc. Prof. Saugata Babu is right here, who is a diabetic himself. I see the challenges that he go through because of the lifestyle. It is a silent killer. Today the whole world is really looking for a solution for diabetes. Nobody knows from where it comes from. Is it necessarily genetic? We have no solution for it. These are issues that we need to talk about. 

Prevention is better than cure. Is awareness really there? Nadda ji just, last week, came out with an outstanding Mental Health Bill. These were not topics which were ever discussed in society. We were ashamed to say if a woman was depressed she was just shunned out or even there was a time when there was post-natal depression. I myself being a woman, even I used to at one time laugh about it. No, there was nothing like post-natal depression. But there is. Some women go through issues like menopause; all women don’t go through it. These are issues which nobody talks in our society. But through the Mental Health Bill, and a lot of other Bills that are coming up today with the Health Ministry, a lot of issues which were swept under the carpet are coming up for discussion.

I am very happy that there are men in this Parliament who are talking about the social issues. The only unfortunate part is, there are lot of Governments which are not addressing like my own Government in Maharashtra has cut today the health budget by about five per cent, which is a substantial amount of money. It is really sad. We used to run a very nice health programme on malnutrition. Earlier, a lot of speakers had spoken about malnutrition in India. We have a group called Citizens Alliance, which has been working for the last seven year. We play a role of a catalyst. We play between the Government and the States to bring in awareness because the root cause of most health problems is nutrition. If we can address the issue of malnutrition, it would really help our next generation. Maharashtra has done a wonderful programme called the Health Mission, which has substantially helped to bring down the number of malnutrition children, especially in tribal areas. If he could intervene, it would be better. We are also requesting the Maharashtra Government to run it. Various other States are looking at it. But if we could take that programme to another level, I think, that would be one of the best services we could do to our next generation. 

The other issue is about doctors. There is a new degree that the Department is coming up with, the B.Sc. in Health – Bachelor in Science. There was a time in 1948 when the Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru ji has banned the degree called RMP. That was like a parallel degree. The thought of that Government was - why have two degrees for doing the same job? That was a time when we had only 11 medical colleges, and still this was banned. Today, we have over 400 medical colleges. I would like the hon. Minister to explain in his reply as to what would the role of B.Sc. in Health be. Would this be like a health guardian or would he have the powers of a doctor? How does a layman know the difference between a doctor and a B.Sc. Health? If you could clarify that, it would be of great help. Nobody is stepping on each other’s role and their role is completely clear. 

It is like our ASHA workers. ASHA workers are really foot soldiers. Even during the debate on the Mental Health Bill, I had requested the hon. Health Minister if he could strengthen the ASHA workers, empower them with more training. Simple things like depression or health issues that women have and who have no access to any public health centres, they are not aware of mental health at all or for that matter, any of the issues concerning women. Even anaemia for that matter is extensively discussed. Anaemia tablets are given when there is a camp. Nobody knows whether the woman consumes the tablet or not. She puts them away; she really does not bother about her own health. It starts with anaemia, anaemia into under-nourished child, under-nourished child into malnutrition. That is again back into a vicious circle. 

So, I would urge the hon. Health Minister to look into this issue as well. If he could connect it all, and bring in, it would be of great help. There are very good ad campaigns going on television. Health was not an issue at one time which was discussed or even glamourised but today, with very good ideas through the Health Ministry, they have brought in very good initiatives by getting good Indian icons to say that TB is an issue, it can be resolved; there is a solution; go and take tablets and it will help. It is really a wonderful initiative – be it vaccination, be it TB or even sanitation issues. 

Maharashtra was the first State which started with sanitation issues. Late R.R. Patil, who was our Rural Development Minister 17 years ago, implemented a programme of Health and Sanitation. At that time, the Maharashtra Government had got an award for Health and Sanitation. Providing water and ensuring sanitation today, however the modern Maharashtra is, in pockets, are still a challenge. As a matter of fact, you will be surprised to know that our Zila Parishad has started a new initiative of cleanliness. … (Interruptions) 

HON. DEPUTY SPEAKER: If you want you can continue your speech tomorrow.

SHRIMATI SUPRIYA SULE : I can just finish in one minute.

I would just ask the hon. Minister to look into the ASHA issues, strengthen them and make more health workers to have a good India. In the 21st century, we need a healthy India. I am sure, with Shri Naddaji at the helm of affairs, we will see a positive difference.
